newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague bourse adds 92 issues to mass delisting.
newsitem.headline: Prague bourse adds 92 issues to mass delisting.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Thursday it added another 92 issues to its original list of hundreds of stocks to be delisted from the bourse due to low activity.
The PSE said in a statement that the last trading day for the first 100 stocks to be delisted would be March 19, while another 392 would finish on April 1.
The bourse has said it would like to delist 800 to 900 issues with the lowest volume of trading and market capitalisation by June.
"The aim of the bourse is to reach a number of traded issues which would bee optimal with regard to the conditions of the Czech capital market," said PSE spokesman Milan Vodicka.
The bourse said the wave of 492 issues to be delisted comprised just 0.41 percent of total trading in the past 12 months.

The exchange is looking at shares which fell into the following three categories according to activity over the last 12 months: 1) Those whose trade turnover was below 200,000 crowns ($7,160). 2) Those with a market capitalisation under five million crowns. 3) Those which traded less than five days on the central market.
Issues which fail to fulfil conditions one and two or one and three would be eligible for de-listing.

There are currently 1,751 shares on the PSE, many of which are small companies which were listed as a direct result of the Czech Republic's massive voucher-for-shares privatisation programme completed in early 1995.
